title: Manager alignment playbook — Lucas Hartman
body:
Purpose / quick note:
- Working doc for manager 1:1 prep and alignment with Maya (skip-level) + direct manager. Focus: concrete evidence of impact, 6–9mo goals, specific asks (coaching/time/resources).
- Keep short bullets for sync; longer context below for follow-up.

Recent wins (evidence + micro-stories):
- Hiring flow improvements: reduced offer-to-accept time from avg 18d -> 10d in pilot team (Sourcing + hiring manager checklists). Evidence: report attached (Q4 hiring-metrics); three hires closed in pipeline conversion experiment.
- Onboarding docs: shipped updated manager checklist + role-specific onboarding templates (eng, product). Observed: new hire survey NPS +7 vs prior cohort (small n = 8).
- Offboarding process: drafted policy that cut access-remediation time to <24h in two trials (SRE + infra). Saved ~12 admin hours over two months.

Areas to highlight in 1:1 (what I want manager to notice):
- Pattern: operational leverage across hiring + onboarding = measurable time savings for managers. Tie that to team capacity metric (FTE-days saved).
- Impact on hiring funnel quality: early data suggests better conversion and clearer expectations -> fewer role mis-hires. Ask for headcount flexibility to scale templates to other teams.

Development goals (6 months):
- Goal 1: Move from operator -> strategic partner for two product orgs. Success metric: being included as stakeholder in 2 product-level planning cycles and cited in retrospective as a constraint removed.
- Goal 2: Build a lightweight analytics dashboard for people ops metrics (time-to-fill, onboarding NPS, access remediation). MVP by end of Q2.
- Goal 3: Coaching: run 4 manager coaching sessions (focus: career conversation, calibration) and solicit structured feedback.

Requests / asks for manager (explicit):
- Time: Block a 60-minute partner sync monthly for product planning touchpoints (explicit calendar commitment).
- Sponsorship: Introduce me to two product managers (names suggested below) for pilot onboarding partnership.
- Budget: small funds (~$6k) to run 2 cohort trainings + tool subscription for lightweight analytics (low friction).
- Signal: help me get invited to the quarterly launch review to present onboarding metrics (1 slide).

Draft agenda for upcoming 1:1 (30 mins):
- 0–5 min: quick personal check-in + priorities
- 5–12 min: 2-minute evidence: hiring + onboarding wins (what changed, numbers)
- 12–22 min: development ask + headcount/budget ask (specific ask + fallback)
- 22–28 min: feedback request (how visible is this work? where to focus?)
- 28–30 min: commitments (who does what next)

Potential objections and my counters:
- "We don't have budget/headcount" -> fallback: pilot in 1 product org; propose reallocation of existing training hours; demonstrate ROI via estimate of reduced manager time per hire.
- "Need more data" -> propose 6-week pilot with lightweight dashboard; I own instrumentation and will provide weekly short notes.

Risks / dependencies:
- Risk: product teams may not prioritize people ops changes; mitigation: secure PM sponsor and present 5-min case in team kickoff.
- Dependency: access to hiring/HR systems for dashboard; need infra help for read-only views (Jira ticket: JIRA-OPS-271).

Follow-up materials to include if asked:
- One-pager: hiring funnel experiment (metrics, methodology, cohort) — attach link to PR in GH.
- Onboarding templates: sample manager checklist + first-week learning path.
- Small ROI calc: time saved * manager hourly rate = potential cost avoidance (template in sheet).

Personal reflection (coaching topics):
- Strengths: systematizing recurring operational work, building trust with hiring managers, translating process changes into measurable outcomes.
- Growth area: shift from doing to enabling (documenting playbooks and training others), better storytelling of impact (concise 1-slide narratives).
- Behavioral ask: help me be more assertive in cross-functional table stakes (how to raise priority without being seen as "nagging").

Quick wins I can commit before next 1:1 (two weeks):
- Prototype dashboard mock in FigJam and share link.
- Draft intro email to two PMs requesting 30m pilot discussion.
- Finalize manager checklist v1 and push to Confluence.

Open questions / prompts for manager input:
- Which PMs or product initiatives should I prioritize for pilot? (suggestions: payments, console rollout, or hosted-api docs team)
- Any preferred timing for manager coaching sessions (day/time constraints)?
- Is there appetite for a small internal brown-bag to socialize onboarding templates?

Notes to self (things to mention verbatim):
- "This pilot is low-effort, high-leverage: 1–2 hours of PM time up front, then templates save manager time repeatedly."
- "If we can demonstrate a clear reduction in time-to-productivity for new hires, it's an easy sell for small budget."

Triage / checklist before the meeting:
- [ ] Attach hiring experiment one-pager
- [ ] Share dashboard mock link (FigJam)
- [ ] Prepare 1-slide ROI summary
- [ ] Draft budget ask line items with alternatives (no-cost options)

End of doc — keep short bullets during meeting; add expanded notes afterwards.

Unfinished / TODO (longer-term):
- Expand onboarding templates to include role-specific micro-learning paths (eng infra, data infra, product ops).
- Build simple automated slack pulse for new hires (week 1, week 4) to collect qualitative signals.
__note: File stored in users/ — personal working doc. Informal tone, granular asks.
